nodes.name: POST /api/agent/run

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ workspace_id: $json.workspace_id, trigger: 'scheduled', cadence: $json.cadence || 'weekly', drive: false }) }}

nodes.notes: Stage 0 only. Returns in well under a minute with the measured numbers already committed, plus `next.lenses` — the list this run intends to execute.

nodes.name: Did it start?
nodes.notes: A run that is already going is someone else's to drive — attaching a second driver would run every lens twice.

nodes.name: POST /api/agent/lens
nodes.notes: One lens per request, run by the agent container next to n8n (AGENT_BASE_URL). NO node-level retry, on purpose: n8n retries a failed HTTP node as a whole, so one lens answering non-2xx re-sent all five and billed every lens twice (run 4de11a81, 2026-09-14: $2.62 instead of ~$1.40). onError=continueRegularOutput passes a failed lens on as its own item instead; the lens route is idempotent per (run_id, lens) and writes an honest failure row, so synthesise still sees every lens. The agent stops a lens at AGENT_LENS_BUDGET_MS; this 10-minute timeout sits above that. batchSize 3 keeps a monthly run's seven lenses from opening seven model calls at once.

nodes.name: POST /api/agent/synthesise
nodes.notes: Answers 409 with the names of any lenses still outstanding — which is why this retries. A 409 is a wait, not a failure, and deliberately does not mark the run failed.

nodes.name: Could not start
nodes.notes: Stage 0 failed — usually Meta credentials. The run row already carries the reason; nothing further to do here.

nodes.name: POST /api/agent/run (app)

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ workspace_id: $json.workspace_id, trigger: 'manual', cadence: $json.cadence || 'weekly', period_days: $json.period_days, drive: false }) }}

nodes.notes: Stage 0 only. Returns in well under a minute with the measured numbers already committed, plus `next.lenses` — the list this run intends to execute.

nodes.name: Answer the app
nodes.notes: Answers the Run button as soon as the numbers are committed, with /run's own reply (run_id, or already_running, or the error). The lenses carry on after this; the page polls research_runs.
